stem:
Myra labels four stomach agents on a science-fair poster: wall movements, digestive juice, acid, and mucus. She must match each to its job: churning food, breaking proteins into simpler components, killing many harmful bacteria, or protecting the stomach lining from acid.

Which matching is correct?

options.text: Wall movements — churning; mucus — protein breakdown; acid — killing bacteria; digestive juice — protecting the lining.
Wall movements — churning; digestive juice — protein breakdown; acid — killing bacteria; mucus — protecting the lining.
Wall movements — churning; digestive juice — protein breakdown; acid — killing bacteria; acid also damages the lining during ordinary digestion.
Wall movements — churning; digestive juice — protein breakdown in the oesophagus; acid — killing bacteria; mucus — protecting the lining.

teacher.key_rationale: Wall movements churn; digestive juice breaks proteins in the stomach; acid kills many harmful bacteria; mucus protects the lining. Mucus does not digest protein; ordinary digestion does not leave the lining unprotected; stomach juice does not act in the oesophagus.
